Title: PDF to Text
Description: Extract the text layer of PDF files into UTF-8 .txt files in your browser, with Unicode font mapping and batch processing. No upload, no OCR.

Seo_Introduction: Extract the text layer of PDF files into plain UTF-8 .txt files in the browser — for search, diffs or feeding text to scripts. Nothing is uploaded and no OCR is involved.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
The extractor reads the text-showing commands of every page and decodes characters through the font's ToUnicode map, the embedded TrueType cmap or WinAnsi encoding, so Cyrillic and other non-Latin text comes out correctly when the PDF provides the mapping. A new line starts wherever the PDF moves to the next line, and pages are separated by a blank line.

Scanned PDFs contain only images and produce empty text, because there is no OCR. Multi-column layouts and tables are flattened in the order the text is stored in the file, and spaces between words depend on how the PDF was produced. Password-protected PDFs are rejected with a clear message.

Add several PDFs at once: they are processed one after another in a Web Worker with a progress bar, **Cancel** stops immediately, and every finished row gets **Download TXT**, which saves `<name>.txt`.
Seo_Examples:
**Two-page document**: a PDF whose pages read “Second doc page A” and “Second doc page B” gives `Second doc page A`, an empty line, `Second doc page B`.

**Large file**: a 2,500-page `5.44 MB` PDF produces a 36 KB `big.txt` while the page stays responsive.

**Scanned contract**: a PDF made of page images gives an empty `.txt` — run OCR elsewhere first.

**Password-protected file**: shows “locked.pdf: the PDF is password-protected and can't be processed.” while the other files in the batch are still extracted.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Add PDF files
Click **Choose file** or drop one or more PDFs onto **Upload PDF**. They appear under **Files to Process**.

### Step 2: Extract
Click **Extract Text**. The progress bar shows the current file; **Cancel** stops the batch.

### Step 3: Download the text
Click **Download TXT** on a row to save `<name>.txt` (UTF-8).
Seo_Tips:
- If the result is empty, the PDF is probably a scan: there is no text layer to extract.
- Garbled characters mean the PDF has no usable Unicode mapping for its font; copying from a PDF viewer will usually fail the same way.
- Tables and columns come out in storage order, so check the line order before parsing the text with scripts.
- Already extracted files are skipped when you click **Extract Text** again, so you can add more files to the same list.
